questions.question: A thief, seeing a policeman from a distance of 120 metres, starts running at a speed of 7 km/h. The policeman chases immediately with a speed of 8 km/h and the thief is caught. What is the distance run by the thief?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance between policemen and thief = 120 m

Speed of the thief = 7 km/h

Speed of policeman = 8 km/h

**Concept Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Relative speed = 8 – 7 = 1 km/h [they are running in the same direction]

⇒ 1 km/h = 1 × (5)/(18) = (5)/(18) m/s

⇒ Time taken to cover 120 m = (120)/(frac{5){18}} = (120 ×18)/(5) = 432 s

⇒ Speed of the thief = 7 km/h = 7 × (5)/(18) = (35)/(18) m/s

⇒ Distance covered by the thief in 432 s = (35)/(18) × 432 = 840 m

**Therefore, thief runs 840 m before he is caught by the policemen**

questions.question: A boat can go 40 km downstream and 25 km upstream in 7 hours 30 minutes. It can go 48 km downstream and 36 km upstream in 10 hours. What is the speed (in km/h) of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Downstream speed = D and Upstream speed = U.

Given time equations: 40/D + 25/U = 7.5 and 48/D + 36/U = 10.

Multiply the first by 6 and the second by 5: 240/D + 150/U = 45 and 240/D + 180/U = 50.

Subtracting yields: 30/U = 5 ⇒ U = 6 km/h. Substituting U back gives D = 12 km/h.

Speed in still water = (D + U) ÷ 2 = (12 + 6) ÷ 2 = 9 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Case 1: Downstream distance = 40 km, Upstream distance = 25 km, Total time = 7.5 hours (15/2 hours).

Case 2: Downstream distance = 48 km, Upstream distance = 36 km, Total time = 10 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Speed of boat in still water = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9626c507ec6d6ba68d11adba02e6430a5c699e4f307d589ddda0802fd86024d5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let downstream speed be D km/h and upstream speed be U km/h.

⇒ From Case 1: 40/D + 25/U = 15/2 ... (i)

⇒ From Case 2: 48/D + 36/U = 10 ... (ii)

⇒ Multiply equation (i) by 6 and equation (ii) by 5 to equalize the D terms:

⇒ 240/D + 150/U = 45 ... (iii)

⇒ 240/D + 180/U = 50 ... (iv)

⇒ Subtracting (iii) from (iv): 30/U = 5 ⇒ U = 6 km/h

⇒ Substitute U = 6 in equation (i): 40/D + 25/6 = 15/2

⇒ 40/D = 15/2 − 25/6 = 45/6 − 25/6 = 20/6 = 10/3

⇒ D = (40 × 3) ÷ 10 = 12 km/h

⇒ Speed of boat in still water = (D + U) ÷ 2 = (12 + 6) ÷ 2 = 18 ÷ 2 = 9 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Downstream & Upstream Concepts

When a boat travels along the direction of the flow of the stream, it is called travelling downstream. When it travels against the flow, it is travelling upstream.

Key Formulas

Speed of Boat in Still Water = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2
Speed of Stream Current = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2

Average Speed

When a boat travels a certain distance upstream and returns the same distance downstream, the overall average speed is calculated as (2 × D × U) ÷ (D + U).

questions.question: A and B run a 12 km race on a circular track of length 1200 m. They complete one round in 300 seconds and 400 seconds, respectively. After how much time from start will the faster person meet the slower person for the last time?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A and B run a 12 km race 

Length of circular track = 1200 m

Time taken by A to complete the first round = 300 seconds

Time taken by B to complete the first round = 400 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time 

**Calculation:**

Here,

We have 12 km i.e. 12000 m race in a circular track of the length of 1200 m.

Number of round to complete the race = 12000/1200 = 10 rounds

Now,

Time taken by A to complete the first round = 300 seconds

For 10 rounds it will take 300 × 10 = 3000 seconds 

Now,

When A and B both start running,

First meet will take place in L.C.M (300,400) seconds = 1200 sec

Next meet will take place = 1200 × 2 = 2400 seconds

For next meet,

Time would be 3600 seconds, which is Not possible as A completes the race in 3000 seconds

But, to complete 10 rounds A takes 3000 seconds. So, time cannot be more than 3000 seconds

So, faster person will meet the slower person last time at 2400 seconds

**Hence, A will meet B last time at 2400 seconds**.

questions.question: Malay walks around a circular field at the rate of 7 rounds per hour, while Neha runs around it at the rate of 11 rounds per hour. They start in the same direction from the same point at 02:45 p.m. They shall first cross each other at:
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

Malay speed round a circular field = 7 rounds per hour.

Neha speed round a circular field = 11 rounds per hour

they start at 2:45 p.m. in the same direction. 

**FORMULA USED:**

Relative speeds when moving in the same direction = difference of speeds.

**CALCULATION :**

The relative speed between Malay and Neha = 11 - 7 = 4 rounds/h (as they are in the same direction )

Time taken to complete one round at this speed = 1/4 hr

⇒ (1/4) × 60 min

⇒ 15 min.

So, 2:45 + 15 min = 3:00 p.m.

**∴ They shall first cross each other after 15 minutes i.e. at 03:00 p.m.**

questions.question: After seeing a policeman from a distance of 500 m, a thief starts running at a speed of 10 km/h. After noticing, the policeman chases immediately with a speed of 12 km/h, and the thief is caught. The distance run by the policeman is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of police = 12 km/h

Speed of thief = 10 km/h

Distance between = 500 m

**Concept used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

Distance between police and the thief = 500m = 0.5 km

let time = x

⇒ 12x = 0.5 + 10x

⇒ 2x = 0.5

⇒ x = 0.25

It will take the policeman 0.25 hours to catch the thief

The thief would have run 0.25 × 10 = 2.5km 

Now Distance traveled by policeman = 12x = 12 × 0.25 = 3 km

**∴ The distance run by the policeman is 3 km.**

questions.question: Anup can row 33 km downstream and 35 km upstream in 8 hours. He can also row 44 km downstream and 28 km upstream in the same time. How much time (in hours) will he take to row 55 km downstream and 14 km upstream?
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

 
 

 
 
Downstream distance

 
 
 
Upstream distance

 
 
 
Time

 
 
 

 
 
33 km

 
 
 
35 km

 
 
 
8 hours

 
 
 

 
 
44 km

 
 
 
28 km

 
 
 
8 hours

 
 
 

 
 
55 km

 
 
 
14 km

 
 
 
 

 
 
 

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of river be “x” and speed of boat be “y”.

Effective downstream speed = x + y

Effective upstream speed = x – y

33over x+y+ 35 over x-y = 8 (Eq. 1)

44over x+y + 28over x-y= 8 (Eq. 2)

Subtracting equation 1 from equation 2-

⇒ 44over x+y - 33over x+y + 28over x-y - 35 over x-y= 0

⇒ 44over x+y - 33over x+y = 35 over x-y - 28over x-y

⇒ 11over x+y = 7over x-y

⇒ 11 × (x - y) = 7 × (x + y)

⇒ 11 x - 11y = 7x + 7y

⇒ 4x = 18y

⇒ x = 9over 2y.

Putting the value of "x" in equation 1-

⇒ 33over {9yover 2}+y + 35over {9yover 2}-y = 8

⇒ 66over 11y + 70over 7y = 8 or 6over y + 10 over y = 8

⇒ y = 2 

Substituting the value of "y" in the value of "x" = 9

∴ Time required for 55 km downstream and 14 km upstream distance = 55over x+y+ 14over x-y

⇒ Time required for 55 km downstream and 14 km upstream distance = 55over 9+2+ 14over 9-2= 5 + 2 = 7 hours

**The total time required for the distance to be traveled is 7 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**Here, according to the question, 

⇒ 33/(x + y) + 35/(x - y) = 8 & 44/(x + y) + 28/(x - y) = 8

As the number of required hours is a complete number hence 

The values of (x + y) & (x - y) should divide the respective numbers

For Downstream, that is 33 and 44 both are multiples of 11

and for Upstream, that is 35 and 28 both are multiples of 7

By value putting method, 

⇒ 33/11 + 35/7 = 3 + 5 = 8 & 44/11 + 28/7 = 4 + 4 = 8

⇒ x + y = 11 & x - y = 7

Required time, 

⇒ 55/11 + 14/7 = 5 + 2 = 7 hours

∴ The total time required for the distance to be traveled is 7 hours.
